I recently finished reading the book, SJWs Always Lie: Taking Down The Thought Police by Vox Day. I know that this sort of post is unusual for /v/neofag, but as I read the book, I realized just how perfectly it describes Gaffots even though they aren't, specifically, the target of the book. It shows how Gaffotry is a symptom of a much wider problem, one that Vox describes as it affected gamers (GamerGate), science fiction fans (the Sad/Rabid Puppies), and miscellaneous other contexts (Brendan Eich, Chick-Fil-A, etc.). For a taste of Vox's insight, you can read this "SJW Attack Survival Guide" for free, which lists Vox's 8 stages of an SJW attack and 8 steps for responding.

But what most caught my eye in the book was its final chapter, titled, "How To Talk to SJWs." Here are some excerpts from that chapter that I think encapsulate the problem with Gaffots' thinking (or lack thereof) (bolding added):

In his book Rhetoric, which is said to be "the most important single work on persuasion every written", the Greek philosopher Aristotle divides the art of persuasion into two distinct forms, dialectic and rhetoric, concerning which he makes a very important observation...: "Before some audiences not even the possession of exactest knowledge will make it easy for what we say to produce conviction. For argument based on knowledge implies instruction, and there are people whom one cannot instruct."

"There are people whom one cannot instruct." One of Man's greatest thinkers, a brilliant teacher who tutored one of history's greatest generals, Alexander the Great, knew that there were people even he could not teach....

However, he went on to point out that it is possible to convince them to change their minds, only that one cannot do so by presenting them with knowledge. Instead, it is necessary to manipulate them and to play upon their emotions in order to get them to change their minds. He even detailed instructions on how to go about communicating with these people who make decisions on the basis of their feelings rather than their logical capacities.

As you can probably guess, SJWs fall squarely into the category of people who cannot be instructed and cannot be convinced by knowledge. This is the key to understanding their astonishing ability to cling to their Narrative in the face of evidence that obliterates it as well as their insistence on clinging to it even as it shifts and contradicts itself. The reason SJWs can believe seven impossible and mutually contradictory things before breakfast is their inability to be instructed by knowledge; as long as each of those seven things happens to be in line with whatever their emotions are at the moment, SJWs will not see the inherent contradictions that thinking people do.

Because they do not think using logic, they cannot speak, or understand, what Aristotle describes as dialectic. Dialectic is based on the construction of logical syllogisms, which therefore makes it very easy to anyone who is capable of following those syllogisms and ascertaining their validity to detect when one is lying. Rhetoric, on the other hand, is "the faculty of observing in any given case the available means of persuasion." Rhetoric is much more forgiving of falsehood, and in fact, it's not even strictly possible to say that a rhetorical statement is a lie. Rhetoric consists of the construction of what Aristotle describes as enthymemes--which are not proper logical syllogisms, but incomplete or invalid arguments that merely take the form of syllogisms--in which all that matters is that persuasion is achieved by means of the "proof" provided, or more accurately, the apparent proof.

Think about how Gaffots argue. When you show that what they say is an example of X (for instance, racism) isn't really an example of X, they'll fall back on the broader argument of, say, "institutional X." It never matters when they're wrong, so long as they follow the narrative. You could demolish every single example of X ever offered, and they would still not abandon their belief that X exists and is a huge problem. In fact, they'd turn it around on you by making a Doctor Who-themed joke about "quantum X" and trying to make anyone feel foolish for questioning whether the topic of discussion is an example of X or not--and that's rhetoric. The rational thing to do when all of your evidence is shown to not support your conclusion is to reject your conclusion, but Gaffots don't think that way. Their conclusion is a given because it's part of the narrative, so it doesn't matter whether any evidence supports it or not, and you're a bigot for questioning whether any evidence supports it!

Hence the importance of knowing your audience and understanding which language of discourse they speak. When you speak in rhetoric to a dialectic-speaker, you will tend to sound very dishonest even when you are utilizing effective rhetoric that is perfectly in line with the truth. On the other hand, you can't speak dialectic to a rhetoric-speaker for the obvious reason that he cannot be informed or persuaded by it. He simply does not have the capacity...

When you speak dialectic to a rhetoric speaker, he hears it as rhetoric. Or, not infrequently, as complete gibberish...

In case it is not already apparent, this chapter is written primarily for dialectic-speakers. Rhetoric-speakers, especially SJWs who are inclined to think badly of me, will only see "blah blah blah, Aristotle, blah blah blah, I'm so smart, blah blah blah, spaghetti spaghetti" and scan through what looks like nothing but a word salad to them trying to find something they can use to minimize or disqualify me.

And that is exactly what an SJW does to you whenever you are trying to communicate with him using logic, reason, and knowledge. Have you ever had an experience where you have clearly laid out a complete train of thought for someone, only to have him stubbornly declare that you are wrong, that you must be wrong, and there is no possibility you could be correct, and doing so without pointing to a single flaw anywhere in your argument? You were speaking the wrong language...

Even SJWs who can more or less understand dialectic don't speak it themselves. That is why they are infamous for never admitting they are wrong even when everyone else can see it, and why they are constantly moving the goalposts and revising the history of what everyone knows actually happened. It is absolutely pointless to speak in dialectic to them; unless you are actually talking to them for the benefit of an audience, there is no reason not to go directly to rhetoric and hammer on their emotions rather than relying on reason to accomplish the impossible.

How many times have we seen Gaffots dismiss a well-reasoned argument as "word salad," or complained that someone was "using a lot of words to say nothing"? That's because they are rhetoric-speakers, and the other person (banned by now, no doubt) was trying to speak to them in dialectic. Like Vox says, it's pointless to try to reason with people with that. And make no mistake, there is no neutral audience to perform to when you post on Gaf, so that can't be a reason to use dialectic either.

But then we get to the problem with following Vox's advice of speaking in rhetoric on Gaf: You'd be banned for it. They'd call it uncivil or trolling if you did it (in fact, that's how Vox defines "trolling" -- "what SJWs call it when you reply to them in their own rhetorical language."), even though it's perfectly acceptable for the narrative-following Gaffots to do it--"Is this the hill you want to die on?" "Tell me more." "You're a racist!" "FOH". If they belittle you (that is, a non-SJW), that's OK because you had it coming. If you belittle them, you're derailing the topic and hey that's an ad hominem and civil inclusive discourse! So, my advice? Don't try to reason with Gaffots. I bought a new computer case for my Plex server and gave my old one away. I never realized how much quieter the new one is over the old one until I had it powered on and working.
Do you have an entire server in your home or something?

Oh no, it's just a desktop. It's just that the software it runs is a "server-client" type software. Plex lets me store movies on my desktop and stream them across my LAN similar to Netflix, with metadata, summaries, and rating information. The best part is that it's my own curated library and it doesn't require internet access since it's only streaming across my LAN. That's actually the only thing I use my desktop for, which is why I don't upgrade the hardware on it very often.
How big of a harddrive do you have?

I have a 6TB internal and a 6TB external as a backup. I currently have about 1700 movies and maybe 130 TV shows, consisting of just over 4TB of data. They all come off of DVDs, so I have several boxes and shelves full of DVDs in storage. It's nice to not have to switch DVDs whenever I watch something, especially with TV shows. The TV shows actually take up the lion's share of the data, since one season of a show is several discs, and most of the shows I watch have several seasons. If you wanted to do just movies, you'd probably use much less space.

The best part is that the popularity of online streaming has dropped the price of DVDs and Blu Rays down, and plenty of people are getting rid of their DVD collections for cheap. And because I get to hand-pick what content to keep in my collection, I never have to worry about what shows Netflix is going to lose the rights to, or what shows they don't have to begin with. The biggest drawback is having to wait for movies to make it to DVD, but that isn't so bad once you get used to it.
